story.iWant: the application to meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards
story.soThat: I can use it with assistive technologies

subtasks.subtask: Install NVDA (Windows) or test VoiceOver setup (Mac)
Run contrast check on all text elements (use axe/WAVE)
Document all contrast violations by page
Fix low-contrast text colors (text-gray-600 → text-gray-700, etc.)
Test in light and dark modes (if applicable)
Verify all fixes meet WCAG 2.1 AA
Tab through each page and document focus order
Identify any keyboard traps or unreachable elements
Fix tab order issues (use tabIndex only when necessary)
Add focus indicators to all interactive elements (ring/outline CSS)
Test modal focus trapping (focus should loop within modal)
Verify all buttons and links functional with keyboard

task.title: Audit & Fix ARIA Labels & Semantic HTML

criterion.title: Color Contrast Compliance
criterion.description: All text meets WCAG 2.1 AA minimum: - Normal text (body, labels): 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum - Large text (18pt+): 3:1 contrast ratio minimum - Graphical elements and UI components: 3:1 contrast ratio minimum - Focus indicators: 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors

criterion.title: Keyboard Navigation & Accessibility
criterion.description: All interactive elements keyboard accessible with logical tab order, visible focus indicators, and no keyboard traps. Form submission possible with Enter key. Modals properly trap focus.

criterion.title: Form Labels & Association
criterion.description: All input fields have properly associated labels via htmlFor attribute. Required fields marked with aria-required. Error messages associated with aria-describedby. No placeholder-only labels. Form instructions programmatically associated.

criterion.title: ARIA Labels & Semantic HTML
criterion.description: Icon-only buttons have aria-label or aria-labelledby. Images have descriptive alt text. Semantic HTML used correctly (nav, main, section, article). Heading hierarchy follows logical order. List items use proper elements. Data tables have proper structure. Form inputs have proper role and state attributes.

criterion.title: Screen Reader Support
criterion.description: Page structure, navigation landmarks, and interactive elements announced correctly. Dynamic content updates announced. Error and success messages announced. Page loading state announced.

criterion.title: Focus Indicators & Visual Feedback
criterion.description: Focus indicators visible on all interactive elements with 2px minimum width, sufficient contrast (3:1 minimum), and not blocked by other elements. Consistent focus outline style across app.

criterion.title: Motion & Animation Accessibility
criterion.description: CSS prefers-reduced-motion: reduce honored. Auto-playing animations can be paused. No content flashing more than 3 times per second. Animation not required to use features.

criterion.title: Accessible Navigation Features
criterion.description: Skip-to-main-content link present and functional. Landmark regions properly used. Breadcrumb trails announced correctly. Sidebar menu structure and state announced. Current page indicator announced with aria-current="page".

criterion.title: Empty & Error States Accessibility
criterion.description: Empty state messaging clear and helpful. Error messages displayed both visually and programmatically. Error message describes problem and solution. Success messages announced when appropriate. Loading state announced.

criterion.title: Responsive & Touch Accessibility
criterion.description: Touch targets minimum 44x44 CSS pixels with adequate spacing. No hover-only functionality. Zoom functionality not disabled. Text resizable without loss of functionality (up to 200%).

tests.standards: Accessibility testing combines automated tools (axe DevTools, WAVE, Lighthouse) with manual testing (keyboard navigation, screen reader testing with NVDA/VoiceOver, contrast verification, mobile touch target testing). Follow WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines and use tools to catch ~40-50% of issues, then conduct thorough manual testing on critical pages.
tests.locations: - Automated audits: Chrome DevTools Lighthouse tab (built-in) - Manual testing: Required on all pages before completion - Integration tests: nextjs-ui/tests/ (if E2E tests use Playwright or Cypress with accessibility plugins) - Accessibility resources: WCAG 2.1 Guidelines (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/), ARIA Authoring Practices (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
tests.ideas: - AC-1 (Contrast): Audit all text with axe/WAVE; verify 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and focus indicators - AC-2 (Keyboard): Tab through all pages; verify logical tab order, visible focus, no traps; test Enter for form submission and Escape for modal close - AC-3 (Forms): Check all inputs have htmlFor labels; verify required fields marked aria-required; test error message association with aria-describedby - AC-4 (ARIA/HTML): Verify icon buttons have aria-label; check images have alt text or role="presentation"; verify semantic HTML (nav, main, section) and heading hierarchy - AC-5 (Screen Reader): Test with NVDA/VoiceOver; verify page structure, landmarks, and interactive element announcements; test dynamic content live regions if needed - AC-6 (Focus): Verify 2px focus outline with 3:1 contrast on all interactive elements; check not obscured by overflow - AC-7 (Motion): Test prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query; verify animations can be paused; check no flashing >3 times/second - AC-8 (Navigation): Verify skip-to-main link; check landmark regions (header, nav, main, aside, footer); test breadcrumb and menu structure with screen reader; verify aria-current="page" - AC-9 (States): Verify empty state, error, success messages announced with aria-live or aria-describedby; test loading state with aria-busy="true" - AC-10 (Mobile): Verify 44x44px touch targets with adequate spacing; test zoom not disabled; verify text resizable to 200% without loss of functionality
